entities.summary: The second most authoritative hadith collection in Sunni Islam, compiled by Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj (c. 815–875 CE) of Nishapur. Containing approximately 7,500 hadith (3,033 without repetitions) selected from 300,000 traditions he examined, Sahih Muslim is praised for its superior organization and arrangement by topic compared to al-Bukhari. Muslim gathered only those traditions where the chain of narrators was continuous and each narrator is documented to have met the next in the chain. The collection is particularly valued for its comprehensive chapters on faith (iman), prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, and eschatology.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sahih Muslim is one of the most authoritative hadith collections in Sunni Islam, containing approximately 7,500 selected traditions that have shaped Islamic theology and practice. Its comprehensive chapters on faith, prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, and eschatology have influenced Islamic scholarship for centuries.
